Subject: Multiple patient sessions aborting — 5xx/429 spike

Marcus —

We started seeing a sudden spike of session aborts and client-side timeouts in our production virtual care flow around 07:40 PDT. Our telemetry shows a sustained 5xx and 429 rate for the streaming/completion endpoint (roughly 18% 5xx and 12% 429 over a 20-minute window). Patients are getting disconnected mid-conversation, and some clients are retrying aggressively which appears to make it worse.

Can your team triage? This is impacting active clinical sessions.

Thanks,
Alex

Alex — thanks for the heads up and the summary. We're escalating to incident ops now.

What we know so far: our real-time metrics are showing a correlated spike in connection churn to the streaming endpoint across a subset of nodes in us-west-2. Initial hypothesis: an interaction between aggressive client retry windows + connection idle timeouts causing request duplication and backlog, leading to upstream 5xx and 429s.

Immediate steps:
- Scheduling an emergency bridge (10 min) to correlate traces and logs — I just sent invites to ops and engineering.
- Can you share a couple of request ids or sample timestamps (UTC) and any client SDK versions in use?
- We'll surface a short mitigation playbook in the bridge (circuit-breaker + throttle at the edge, temporary raise keepalive, reduce default client retry).

I'll be on the call.

—Marcus

> - Scheduling an emergency bridge (10 min) to correlate traces and logs — I just sent invites to ops and engineering.

All — joining bridge now. Quick notes from infra: autoscaler on the affected GPU pool saw a burst of short-lived connections that didn't complete KV cache warmup; the dispatcher queued a backlog and started returning 503/504s under pressure. Edge rate limiter then returned 429s to clients.

Short mitigation I'm pushing now:
1) Enable temporary 5-minute client-side retry jitter (recommend clients add exponential backoff; we can flip a flag in the SDK docs).
2) Adjust keepalive on the gateway to 90s to reduce premature idle disconnects (temporary).
3) Route new traffic to the warm pool (us-west-1 spare capacity) while we stabilize.

I'll post playbook steps and attach the trace bundle.

-Jordan

Date: 2027-06-22T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: mitigation playbook and logs

Alex —

Thanks for the quick collaboration on the bridge. We implemented the following during the first mitigation window (08:45–09:15 PDT):
- Traffic re-route: 22% of new sessions moved to warm pool in us-west-1.
- Edge throttling: soft 50 qps throttle per client key for 20 minutes.
- Gateway keepalive increased to 90s for affected frontends.
- SDK recommended change: client retry capped at 3 attempts with 200–800ms exponential jitter.

Preliminary outcome: 5xx rate dropped from ~18% to ~6% and 429s to ~3% in the affected window; however, we still observed isolated idle disconnects and a secondary retry burst around 10:20 PDT.

I've attached logs and a short runbook (runbook_session_abort_v2.pdf) with exact commands and rollback steps. We recommend Brightwell apply the SDK retry cap and update the keepalive to match the temporary gateway change.

Evelyn Hart
Senior Incident Manager, Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-06-23T14:50:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary and executive note — Brightwell Health session abort wave (June 22)

Team —

Summary (short): On 2027-06-22 we observed a cascading failure pattern driven by a combination of aggressive client retry logic and premature connection idle timeouts. The retry amplification led to dispatcher backlog and transient 5xx/429 responses which increased client retries in a feedback loop.

Actions taken:
- Immediate routing to warm pool and edge throttling reduced error rates by ~65% within the first mitigation window.
- Temporary gateway keepalive increase and SDK retry cap were recommended to Brightwell; they rolled the SDK change to a staged subset of users.
- We performed a rolling configuration change to accept longer-lived connections on affected frontends and added a circuit-breaker at the edge to collapse repetitive bursts from identical client keys.

Follow-up items (owner):
- Engineering: implement automatic retry-mitigation middleware (Jordan) — ETA 2 weeks.
- SDK: default retry capped and docs update (Laura) — ETA 3 days.
- CS/Customer: coordinated post-mortem with Brightwell and exec summary (Marcus/Evelyn) — scheduled 2027-06-24 11:00 PDT.

Impact: customer-facing incidents lasted ~90 minutes at peak; no PHI was exposed. Brightwell's CTO requested an executive brief which is scheduled. Financial impact under review; account rep will update deal notes.

I'll attach the final artifact and share the brief after the post-mortem.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
